A.objects: Probability measures P and Q; real transition tables p and q; a real budget B; a stopping time τ; a nonnegative extended-real observable W; and an existential real-valued function L.
A.domains: The path space S is ℕ → Bool with the product measurable structure and discrete Bool. H n = Fin n → Bool. The tables p and q have type (n : ℕ) → H n → Bool → ℝ. F n is the σ-algebra pulled back by the length-n prefix map, reading coordinates 0 through n−1. The maps have types τ : S → WithTop ℕ, W : S → ENNReal, and L : S → ℝ.
A.quantifiers: The conclusion holds for every choice of P, Q, p, q, B, τ, W and the stated hypotheses. Both table normalizations apply to every n and h, including histories of zero mass. The budget is for every n, P-almost every x. One L satisfies the entire conjunction; the likelihood convergence and L's nonnegativity are P-almost everywhere, and the conclusion about τ being finite is Q-almost everywhere.
A.assumptions: P and Q are probability measures. R₁ P p and R₁ Q q give the recursion a(M,n+1,snoc(h,b)) = a(M,n,h)·t n h b for all n,h,b for the respective measure/table pairs, where a is the real prefix-event mass. R₂ P p q requires p n h b = 0 to imply q n h b = 0 whenever a(P,n,h)>0. Each table is nonnegative on Bool and sums to 1 at every history. For each n, ∑_{k<n} E P p q k x ≤ B for P-almost every x. τ is an F-stopping time and τ≠⊤ P-almost everywhere. W is measurable and its nonnegative extended integral of W² under P is finite.
A.conclusion: There exists a strongly measurable L with 0 ≤ L P-almost everywhere and MemLp L 2 P. For P-almost every x, D P Q n x converges to L x as n tends to infinity. The real integrals satisfy ∫L² dP ≤ exp B and ∫L dP = 1. As measures, Q = P.withDensity (x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (L x)), and Q is absolutely continuous with respect to P. The set {x | τ x ≠ ⊤} is measurable and has full Q-measure. Both nonnegative extended integrals of W, under P and under Q separately, are finite. The absolute difference of their real conversions is at most √((exp B−1)·variance_P(x ↦ (W x).toReal)).
A.senses: D is Q-prefix mass divided by P-prefix mass, with real division by zero equal to zero. E is zero at histories of zero P-prefix mass; elsewhere it is the Bool sum of (q−p)²/p at the observed history, using that same division convention. The budget controls cumulative discrepancy P-almost surely at each finite horizon, not on every path and not merely in expectation. The likelihood is indexed by the deterministic prefix length n, not by τ. The assumptions do not require W to depend on τ or be measurable at τ. Absolute continuity is Q≪P only, and the Q-integrability assertion is first-moment finiteness of W, not a Q-second-moment assertion. The explicit finiteness conclusions make the conversions of both W integrals meaningful as finite reals rather than using the convention ⊤.toReal = 0.
A.constants: Prefix depth zero is empty; finite sums use k=0,…,n−1. Normalization and mean density are 1, the Lp exponent and square powers are 2, and the two bounds use exp B and exp B−1 respectively. The excluded stopping-time value is ⊤. B is real and there is no separate nonnegativity assumption on B.

B.objects: A real parameter m; scalars p=(m²)⁻¹ and q=m⁻¹; the specified tables pt=U p p and qt=U q 1; the specified observable C m; the constant stopping time x↦2; and existential measures P and Q.
B.domains: P and Q are measures on S = ℕ → Bool with the product measurable structure. Table arguments are n : ℕ, h : H n = Fin n → Bool, b : Bool, with real values and the same prefix filtration F. C m : S → ENNReal. The constant stopping time takes the value 2 in WithTop ℕ.
B.quantifiers: For every real m with 2≤m, there exist P and Q jointly satisfying the full conjunction. Each table is normalized at every n and h, with nonnegativity for every b. Separately for each of P and Q, almost every path has x k = false for every k≥2. The strict bound on the sum of discrepancy integrals holds for every n.
B.assumptions: The only external hypothesis is 2≤m. The scalars and tables are let-bound from m: U u v assigns true-probability u at depth zero, v at depth one if the first bit is true and zero there otherwise, and zero at all depths at least two; false-probability is the complement. Probability, recursion, compatibility, normalization, and stopping properties are required of the witnesses in the conclusion, not assumed as inputs.
B.conclusion: There are probability measures P and Q with R₁ P pt, R₁ Q qt and R₂ P pt qt. Both pt and qt are nonnegative on Bool and sum to 1 at all histories. The constant map x↦2 is an F-stopping time. Under P and under Q separately, all coordinates k≥2 are false almost surely. For every n, ∑_{k<n} ∫ E P pt qt k x dP(x) < 2, using ordinary real integrals. The map C m is measurable, ∫⁻ (C m)² dP = 1, and ∫⁻ C m dQ = ENNReal.ofReal m.
B.senses: R₁ is the prefix mass recursion and R₂ is the one-sided support condition only at positive-P-mass histories. E uses the same zero-mass and real division conventions as in A. The strict bound is on sums of P-integrals of E, not a P-almost-sure bound on sums along paths. C m pays ENNReal.ofReal(m²) if coordinates 0 and 1 are both true and zero otherwise; it is a terminal charge, not an observation count. The constant stopping time and the almost-sure restrictions on later coordinates are separate facts. The stated moment equalities concern the P second moment and the Q first moment; there is no asserted likelihood limit, density, or variance bound.
B.constants: The scalar threshold is m≥2; the table parameters are ((m²)⁻¹,(m²)⁻¹) for pt and (m⁻¹,1) for qt. The stopping value and tail cutoff are both 2, and the discrepancy cap is strictly less than 2 at every horizon. The P second moment is exactly 1, the Q first moment is exactly ENNReal.ofReal m, and the charge on the two-true prefix is ENNReal.ofReal(m²).
